mbm-0268.clue: The map fits behind my watch strap.
mbm-0268.quote: I drew the route from the station to the old baths on a strip of paper. It rained, and the ink ran everywhere except one blue dot. I found the baths by following the smell of hot stone.

mbm-0269.quote: Our usual percussionist came to the son session straight from a trip. He kept time on his closed suitcase. My favorite recording still has a soft little jingle from the keys on the handle.

mbm-0270.clue: We call the yellow buoy breakfast.
mbm-0270.quote: I paddle out before breakfast and turn at the yellow buoy. My brother once met me there in his kayak with a net full of peaches. For once breakfast came exactly on time.

mbm-0271.clue: You’ve probably seen my left elbow.
mbm-0271.quote: They filmed a street scene outside our local cinema. I queued up three nights in a row to spot myself in the crowd. All you see is an elbow holding popcorn, but that popcorn is definitely mine.

mbm-0272.clue: I tell the ending to the kettle.
mbm-0272.quote: When a sentence won’t sit still I read it aloud while the water heats. If I get the last word in before the whistle, I keep it. My shortest story made very good tea.

mbm-0273.clue: The letter is stitched in small blue squares.
mbm-0273.quote: My grandmother sent a postcard from the mountains with one big cloud in the corner. I copied it into a quilt, down to the crooked little stamp. The mail carrier got to see it first.

mbm-0274.clue: I leave some daylight in the jar.
mbm-0274.quote: I photograph jam jars on our windowsill after everybody’s had breakfast. Red light comes through the raspberry and golden light comes through the peach. My favorite negative is almost all toast crumbs.

mbm-0275.clue: The trick is to listen to the bells.
mbm-0275.quote: I sewed little bells into the corners of my juggling scarves. At the top of the throw they go quiet together. That tiny gap is when I know to look the audience in the eye.

mbm-0276.clue: My loudest puppet has a whispering part.
mbm-0276.quote: I stitched a dragon glove puppet with bright green whiskers. He opens our show by leaning right down to the front row and whispering the password. I can hear the kids whisper it back through the stage.

mbm-0277.clue: I keep a wing in my coat pocket.
mbm-0277.quote: It’s a balsa wing from the first glider I built. When I watch the planes land I tilt it like their wings. A mechanic saw me and showed me how the flaps really move.

mbm-0278.clue: I give my characters grocery money.
mbm-0278.quote: I couldn’t write a scene in a market until I drew up a shopping list for the hero. He bought two lemons and spent the rest on a canary. I had to rewrite the last four pages for the bird.

mbm-0279.clue: I practice on the porch so the ceiling can rest.
mbm-0279.quote: I tried a new juggling trick indoors and left a faint orange circle in the ceiling paint. Mum suggested a leaf, so I painted one. We take every visitor to see our famous ceiling orange.

mbm-0280.clue: The third tent peg is always the loudest.
mbm-0280.quote: My friend sleeps until he hears me tap the coffee pot with a tent peg. I made breakfast quietly once and he slept through the whole sunrise. I save the peg a seat by the pot now.

mbm-0281.clue: That blue bridge is on my map twice.
mbm-0281.quote: I rode out along one canal bank and back on the other. The little bridge I drew twice turned out to be the same one seen in two reflections. I kept both bridges on the map.

mbm-0282.clue: It looks like a plain border from the top.
mbm-0282.quote: I stitched a line of empty chairs round our family quilt. Every time someone comes for supper I embroider one little plate. We’ve had to add another tablecloth at the corner.

mbm-0283.clue: We bow to the broom before we go home.
mbm-0283.quote: I stayed after class to sweep with my teacher. He turned the broom to show me how my shoulders had been twisting in a form. That dusty floor taught me more than the mirror.

mbm-0284.quote: I count the door numbers down the steep part of my route. The day I made it all the way back up without stopping, I rang my friend’s bell at number one just to tell her.

mbm-0285.clue: The thunderstorm fits in an umbrella stand.
mbm-0285.quote: For our school reunion play I painted a rolled backdrop to look like a storm. Between acts it stands by the door with the umbrellas. One wet night a guest nearly carried off the weather.

mbm-0286.clue: It’s the only tee on the key ring.
mbm-0286.quote: I put the wooden tee from my first round with Mum on my keys. She can hear me coming down the path to the clubhouse. Last Sunday she’d poured the tea before I touched the door.

mbm-0287.quote: I juggle three wooden spoons for our kitchen talent show. The long one turns more slowly. I catch it by the bowl and everybody thinks I meant to add a flourish.

mbm-0288.clue: The song starts with a door closing.
mbm-0288.quote: My cousin records our singing on cassette. On our favorite take the tea cupboard shuts right on beat one. We have tried a dozen cleaner versions and none of them dance like that cupboard.

mbm-0289.clue: My favorite postcard shows half a roof.
mbm-0289.quote: I sketched a rooftop garden while our sightseeing bus waited at a light. The light turned green before I finished. I walked the route the next day to find out what grew on the other half.

mbm-0290.clue: My uncle calls it the breakfast rhythm.
mbm-0290.quote: He taught me the son clave while the coffee brewed, two spoons tapping the edge of a wooden tray. When I got it right he slid my cup across on the last beat.

mbm-0291.clue: The grey in that wall is a funny mixture.
mbm-0291.quote: I set out to paint the stone wall behind our house. The cat slept in the same place so long that the grey paint ran out first. Her sunny patch on my canvas is the color of my last cold coffee.

mbm-0292.clue: The curl is stitched into the side.
mbm-0292.quote: My gran asked for a bag for her curlers. I crocheted it in spirals so nobody could mistake it for her tea cozy. She fills it with peppermints when she travels and lets people guess.
